title: Spaghetti and homemade meatballs

items: 1 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)

steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
In a large bowl, soak the breadcrumbs in the milk 5 min. Add the beef, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley, salt and pepper and mix gently with your hands just until combined. Overmixing makes them tough.
Roll into 1½-inch balls (about 18) and set them 1 inch apart on the pan. Wet your hands if the mixture sticks.
Bake 15–18 min, until browned and the center of a meatball reads 160°F.
While they bake, bring a large pot of water to a boil and add 1 Tbsp salt. Warm the marinara in a 12-inch skillet over medium-low heat.
Add the baked meatballs to the sauce, cover and simmer over low heat 10 min, turning them once.
Meanwhile, cook the spaghetti until al dente. Save ½ cup of pasta water, drain, and toss the spaghetti with a few spoonfuls of sauce and a splash of the water.
Serve the spaghetti topped with meatballs, more sauce and lots of parmesan.
tips: Freeze extra baked meatballs on the sheet pan, then bag them. Simmer them from frozen in sauce, covered, about 20 min, until they reach 165°F.
For a browner crust, sear the baked meatballs in 1 Tbsp oil over medium-high heat 2–3 min before they go into the sauce.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days with the meatballs in the sauce; keep the spaghetti separate. Freeze meatballs in sauce up to 3 months. Reheat covered on the stove over medium-low heat until the meatballs reach 165°F.
